android.desc:
Detectify hidden devices detector is a privacy inspection toolkit designed to help you check for unfamiliar electronics and hidden devices using Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, magnetic field and infrared camera tools.

With Detectify, you can scan spy bugs and nearby wireless devices, review unfamiliar Wi-Fi and Bluetooth devices, monitor magnetic field changes, inspect unusual infrared light sources and follow checks for common hiding places.

Hidden Devices Detector
Detectify combines multiple device detection and inspection tools in one app. Use Wi-Fi scanning, Bluetooth detection, magnetic field readings, IR camera inspection and manual checks to investigate unfamiliar electronics and wireless devices around you.

Wi-Fi Device Scanner
Scan devices visible on your connected Wi-Fi network and review available device information. Unfamiliar devices can then be checked more closely through physical inspection.

Bluetooth Device Detector
Detectify - Detect hidden devices helps you discover nearby Bluetooth devices and review approximate signal proximity. Select a device and monitor signal changes as you move around the area.

Bluetooth proximity is an estimate and may be affected by walls, interference, device hardware and surrounding conditions.

Magnetic Field Detector
Use your phone's magnetometer to check changes in magnetic activity around nearby objects. Detectify includes a magnetic field meter and live graph so you can monitor readings in real time.

Higher readings may also be caused by speakers, wiring, magnets, phones, appliances, metal objects and other electronics. Treat magnetic readings as indicators, not proof of a hidden device.

IR Camera Detector
Use your phone's camera and visual filters to inspect dark areas for unusual infrared light sources. Some cameras and electronic devices may emit IR light that can appear differently through a phone camera.

Results depend on your phone's camera hardware, lighting conditions and surrounding environment.

Hidden Camera Inspection
Detectify provides multiple tools for inspecting unfamiliar rooms for possible hidden cameras and electronic devices. Use the IR camera detector, Wi-Fi scanner, Bluetooth scanner and magnetic field detector together with careful physical inspection.

Bluetooth Proximity Tracking
Select a nearby Bluetooth device and follow changes in approximate signal proximity while moving around.

quotes.text:
So no reason that driverless cars can't be misused lots of other ways, by everyone.  Sending bombs, civilians spying on government and police, anyone spying on anyone, stalking, sale of illicit items, and more I'm sure.  The real problem is the cameras, not the cars.  Anyone can put a camera anywhere and make it mobile by attaching it to anything mobile.

An automated camera detector (which looks for light reflection off a camera lens) would be useful as a cheap, easily available tool.  You can get cheap manual ones on eBay.  An augmented reality one should be possible to build as a cell phone app.  Maybe one exists already?  Yes, they do:

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hiddencamdetect.techcamdetect&gl=US

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.wondertechstudio.hiddendevicedetectorandcameradetector&gl=US

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hidden-camera-detector/id532882360

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/spycam-detector/id1507203634

Easy to dedicate a cheap phone to detect cameras everywhere.

The other issue is who gets to decide what the police can do?  This comes up over and over, where the police see there is nothing preventing them from doing something so they do it, regardless of whether it is a good idea for society and with no oversight.  We don't just need laws regulating what the police (and CIA and NSA, and DHS, President, Senate, House, town officials, etc.) do _after_ they do something bad, we need live, real time oversight of decision …
quotes.story_title: San Francisco police use driverless cars for surveillance
